symptom: `mxcli marketplace update <id> --to <v> --save-edits <dir>` saves only elements owned by the module being replaced; an association a LOCAL module owns that points at an entity of the marketplace module (e.g. a local Config entity linked to the module's Settings entity) is not saved, the update proceeds without --force because the module itself is unedited, and afterwards the association is gone and Studio Pro reports the missing association (mendixlabs/mxcli#1502).
cause: Not merely a save gap: the update DESTROYS the association. `PerformUpdate` runs DROP MODULE, which deletes the module's entities, and `DeleteEntity` (mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_alter.go) cascades into every other domain model, removing cross-module associations whose TO end names the deleted entity. `SnapshotModule` enumerated only `objects WHERE ModuleName = <module>`, so the comparison, the gate and --save-edits never saw an element stored in another module. Fixed by `Snapshot.Dependents` (catalog `associations` view: other module, FROM/TO prefixed `<module>.`, matched with substr since `_` is a LIKE wildcard), carried as `Report.Dependents`, saved as `association-<Module>_<Name>.mdl`, counted by `gateOnLocalEdits`, listed in `marketplace diff` and the update summary.
insight: The question to ask of any replace-a-module path is not 'what does the module contain' but 'what does deleting it cascade into' — read DeleteEntity's cascade before trusting a module-scoped enumeration. The cheapest proof is a two-line characterisation test (create the cross association, PerformUpdate, DESCRIBE it fails) on the vendored expr-checker fixture, which has MyFirstModule beside Administration; it doubles as the control that something was at risk. Keep dependents OUT of LocallyModified: they are not edits to the marketplace module, and reporting them as such would make `diff` accuse the module of a change the user made elsewhere — gate on them separately. The saved replay creates the association with a new GUID, so link data is not guaranteed to survive; preserving the association's raw BSON across the drop is the real fix and is not done here.
